title: Elastic IP versus ephemeral public IP
hook: An Elastic IP (EIP) is a static public IPv4 address you allocate to your account until you release it. An ephemeral public IP is auto-assigned when an instance launches in a public subnet and disappears when the instance stops — unless replaced by an Elastic IP association.

blocks.text: Elastic IPs persist across stop/start cycles and can move between instances or network interfaces. NAT Gateways require an Elastic IP. Ephemeral public IPs come from Amazon pool when MapPublicIpOnLaunch is true or you associate a public IP at launch — stopping the instance releases it (classic behavior). Elastic IPs incur charge when allocated but not associated. IPv6 addresses are generally public and behave differently — foundation focus is IPv4 EIP vs ephemeral.

blocks.text: Partners whitelist Elastic IPs for B2B integrations. NAT Gateway stability depends on EIP. Accidentally relying on ephemeral IP for DNS A record breaks on stop. Best practice: no public IP on app tier — ALB DNS name is stable; EIP only for NAT and rare static requirements.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: EIP persists and costs when idle; ephemeral changes on stop. NAT needs EIP. App tier uses ALB — no public IP on EC2.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Launch in public subnet
items.body: MapPublicIpOnLaunch assigns ephemeral public IP if no EIP.

items.title: Allocate EIP
items.body: aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc creates static IP in account pool.

items.title: Associate EIP
items.body: Bind to instance or ENI — replaces ephemeral mapping.

items.title: Stop instance
items.body: Ephemeral released; EIP stays in account, reassociates on start.

diagram.title: EIP vs ephemeral lifecycle
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  Launch[Instance launch] --> EPH[Ephemeral public IP]
  Launch --> EIPalloc[Allocate EIP]
  EIPalloc --> ASSOC[Associate to ENI]
  Stop[Stop instance] --> REL[Ephemeral released]
  Stop --> KEEP[EIP retained in account]
  NAT[NAT Gateway] --> REQEIP[Requires EIP always]

snippet.label: Allocate and associate Elastic IP
snippet.code:
ALLOC=$(aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc --query AllocationId --output text)
aws ec2 associate-address \
  --instance-id i-0abc123 \
  --allocation-id $ALLOC
snippet.explanation: Domain vpc is required for VPC instances — ec2-classic domain is legacy. Association replaces ephemeral public IP.

snippet.label: EIP for NAT Gateway
snippet.code:
NatElasticIp:
  Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
  Properties:
    Domain: vpc
    Tags:
      - Key: Name
        Value: nat-gateway-eip-az-a
NatGateway:
  Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
  Properties:
    AllocationId: !GetAtt NatElasticIp.AllocationId
    SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetA
snippet.explanation: NAT Gateway cannot use ephemeral IP — EIP is mandatory. Tag EIPs for cost and ownership audits.

snippet.label: Find unassociated Elastic IPs (cost leak)
snippet.explanation: Unassociated EIPs bill hourly — release after decommissioning NAT or bastions.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Pointing customer DNS A record at EC2 ephemeral IP. Leaving unassociated EIPs after teardown. Exceeding default EIP quota per Region. Using EIP on every app server instead of ALB.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: Config rule ec2-eip-attached; weekly describe-addresses for orphans; partner whitelist doc listing NAT EIPs only. Auto Scaling complicates EIP — use ALB for inbound, not EIP on ASG instances. Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) for portable ranges — rare, enterprise. IPv6: no EIP equivalent; use stable ALB AAAA or Global Accelerator.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: No EIP management on app tier
Prefer SSM Session Manager — no public IP
Document for partner egress allow lists

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Public EIP on every Auto Scaling instance for 'stable IP.' Strong answer: ALB for inbound stability, EIP only for NAT and documented exceptions, release orphans.

interviewTakeaways: Elastic IP is static until released; ephemeral public IP changes when instance stops (unless EIP associated).
NAT Gateway requires Elastic IP; application tier should use load balancer DNS, not instance public IP.
Unassociated Elastic IPs cost money — audit and release unused allocations.
60s: EIP persists, ephemeral does not. NAT needs EIP. App uses ALB. No EIP on ASG instances.
Follow-up: how does BYOIP differ from Elastic IP?
commonPitfalls: DNS A record to EC2 ephemeral IP gets you rejected — use ALB alias or EIP with failover plan.
Strong answer: EIP for NAT/partner whitelist; ALB for user traffic; release unused EIPs.
Forgetting Domain vpc on allocate-address — wrong pool type.
Stopping dev instance and wondering why SSH IP changed.
